result.title: From atomic events to material degradation across metre and year scales
result.summary: Material degradation emerges from microscopic events whose consequences accumulate over years, yet mechanism-resolved simulations remain confined below engineering timescales. The challenge is not just the sheer number of events: atomistic evolution is dominated by recurrent local motion, with only a tiny fraction driving lasting structural change. This distinction is not encoded in an instantaneous atomic configuration. Locally indistinguishable states can exhibit different event competition, escape times, and long-horizon outcomes, revealing missing kinetic context as a critical information bottleneck. This context spans space and time: the future consequence of a local transition depends on its surrounding defect environment and the kinetic history leading to its current state. To solve this, AtomWorld reconstructs a predictive kinetic state from multiscale structural observations and trajectory history, distinguishing transient fluctuations from microscopic pathways that drive persistent structural evolution. Learning operates only over transitions admitted by the underlying kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) process, preserving event legality, state evolution, and physical time. Across BCC Fe-Cu precipitation, FCC Ni-Cr-Al ordering, and HCP Zr-H interstitial transport, restoring kinetic context consistently advances persistent evolution while maintaining physical fidelity and transferring to unseen conditions. In irradiated reactor-pressure-vessel steel, this approach achieves up to 420-fold greater persistent evolution under matched event budgets. Combined with scalable execution, it successfully extends mechanism-resolved trajectories to service-year timescales across metre-scale heterogeneous domains.

AI.brief_summary: 面向材料降解的跨尺度模拟，提出 AtomWorld，从多尺度结构观测与轨迹历史中重建「动力学预测状态」，以区分瞬时涨落与驱动持久结构演化的微观路径，并在保持 KMC 事件合法性的约束下学习状态转移。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「瞬时构型不足以判断后果、需由历史重建预测状态」的信息瓶颈论述，可能与 LVR 中单次视觉观测不足、需在 latent 状态中积累并筛选证据的问题同构，可供核查状态抽象与瞬态/持久信号分离的表述。
